title: NFR-001 Least privilege: no tool outside the assigned allowlist can be called
risk: An agent reaches a tool that was never granted, for example a raw database writer or an invoice API, and performs an action outside any authority model.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
SAL-02 is granted the read and message skills only; the allowlist is resolved server-side per agent.

steps.action: Call each of the three ungranted tools through the agent runtime
steps.expected: Every call is refused before dispatch with a typed denial; no adapter is invoked.
Each names the tool and the reason (not on allowlist or prohibited), and records the agent identity.

steps.action: Call a granted tool for contrast
steps.expected: The granted read succeeds, proving the allowlist does not simply block everything.

assertions: Zero of the three ungranted tools reach their adapter; the adapters expose call counters that all read 0.
Refusals are typed and audited, not generic 500s.
The granted tool still works, so the control is a boundary and not a blanket outage.
No test exists that passes by circumventing the boundary: the case itself asserts the bypass fails.
forbidden: Widening the allowlist at runtime from agent-provided input.
Treating an unknown tool as allowed.
Suppressing the denial so the caller sees success.
evidence: Denial records for all three attempts with tool names and reasons.
Adapter call counters showing zero invocation.
Successful granted-tool call as the contrast evidence.
cleanup: Delete gov- attempt rows and namespace keys.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state.
